# ui::AnimatedVisualSource

Header: `winui/render/AnimatedVisualSource.hpp`.

The content an [AnimatedVisualPlayer](../controls/animated-visual-player.md#uianimatedvisualplayer) plays: an animation with a fixed size and length whose [render_frame()](#render_frame) draws any point of it through [Renderer](renderer.md).

Implement it: draw your animation in [render_frame()](#render_frame) and hand it to an [AnimatedVisualPlayer](../controls/animated-visual-player.md#uianimatedvisualplayer).

A source has a fixed natural size and total duration, and [render_frame()](#render_frame) draws the frame at a progress point. [AnimatedVisualPlayer](../controls/animated-visual-player.md#uianimatedvisualplayer) and [AnimatedIcon](../controls/animated-icon.md#uianimatedicon) hold a non-owning `const AnimatedVisualSource*`, so the caller keeps the source alive at least as long as any player or icon points at it. [render_frame()](#render_frame) is const and depends only on `progress`, so one instance can serve many players at once.

Example: 
```cpp
class Pulse final : public ui::AnimatedVisualSource
{
public:
    [[nodiscard]] ui::Size natural_size() const override { return {24.0f, 24.0f}; }
    [[nodiscard]] ui::Duration duration() const override { return ui::Duration{900.0}; }
    void render_frame(ui::Renderer& r, const ui::Rect& bounds, double progress) const override
    {
        const float radius = std::min(bounds.width, bounds.height) * 0.5f * static_cast<float>(progress);
        if (radius > 0.0f)
        {
            r.fill_ellipse(bounds.center(), radius, radius, ui::Color::from_rgba(0, 120, 215));
        }
    }
};

static const Pulse pulse; // must outlive the player
window.set_content(ui::AnimatedVisualPlayer{.source = &pulse, .width = 96, .height = 96});
```

## ~AnimatedVisualSource

```cpp
virtual ~AnimatedVisualSource() = default
```

## natural_size

```cpp
virtual Size natural_size() const = 0
```

The unstretched size this source draws at, in DIPs. [AnimatedVisualPlayer](../controls/animated-visual-player.md#uianimatedvisualplayer) fits it into its bounds per its [Stretch](namespace-ui.md#stretch) with [fit_stretch()](namespace-ui.md#fit_stretch), as [Image](../controls/image.md#uiimage) does for a bitmap.

## duration

```cpp
virtual Duration duration() const = 0
```

How long one full [0,1] progress sweep takes, in milliseconds like every other duration in the library ([Theme::anim_normal](../themes/theme.md#anim_normal), [ToolTipControl::delay()](../controls/tool-tip.md#delay)). A source made from an animation file reads it from the file. A source with no length, such as a pose that never moves, can return 0, which [AnimatedVisualPlayerControl::duration()](../controls/animated-visual-player.md#duration) handles.

## render_frame

```cpp
virtual void render_frame(Renderer& renderer, const Rect& bounds, double progress) const = 0
```

Draws one frame at normalized `progress` (0 = animation start, 1 = animation end) into `bounds`. It is called from render(), so what it draws may depend only on `progress` and the source's own fixed state, and it changes nothing, like every [Element::render()](../tree/element.md#render).

## available

```cpp
virtual bool available() const
```

Whether this source can be shown at all. A source that depends on something the running system lacks returns false, and [AnimatedVisualPlayer](../controls/animated-visual-player.md#uianimatedvisualplayer) shows its fallback content instead.
